# Component Reference

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/build_reference.py` from `sensoryforge describe --json`. Do not edit: change the code,
then run the command again. -->

Every neuron model, filter, stimulus, solver, grid arrangement, receptive-field builder and processing layer that SensoryForge registers, with its parameters, defaults, ranges and units.

This page is generated from the component registries and from each component's `ParamSpec` list, so a name, default, range or unit here is the component's own. `sensoryforge describe --json` prints the same data for a program ([Describing SensoryForge to a program](../user_guide/describe.md)). The page lists the components that ship with SensoryForge; a plugin's components appear in `sensoryforge describe` once the plugin is installed. A component you add to SensoryForge appears here after `python scripts/build_reference.py`, and a test fails until it does.

## Reading the tables { #reading }

- **Names.** A name is matched without regard to case. Names under one heading are the same component.
- **Default.** Written as YAML writes it: `null` is unset, a string is quoted.
- **Range.** The smallest and largest value the parameter allows, or the choices it allows.
- **Unit.** Empty means the parameter is dimensionless.
- **Advanced.** The GUI shows an advanced parameter only when its **Advanced** toggle is on.
- **No `ParamSpec`.** A component that declares none has a table of its constructor arguments instead. That is not a component with no arguments.

## Neuron models { #neuron }

Written as the `neuron_model` of a population.

A default below is the model's own. For a model that has type presets, a population starts from the preset its `neuron_type` selects and applies `model_params` on top, so the values a population runs can differ from these defaults (`resolve_neuron_params` in `sensoryforge/config/defaults.py`).

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`AdEx`](#neuron-adex) | Adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire neuron (batched PyTorch). |
| [`dsl`](#neuron-dsl), `DSL (Custom)` | Parse neuron model equations and compile to PyTorch nn.Module. |
| [`FA`](#neuron-fa) | Fast-adapting tactile neuron with explicit amplifier/threshold stages. |
| [`Izhikevich`](#neuron-izhikevich) | Project-compatible Izhikevich neuron with optional parameter noise. |
| [`level_crossing`](#neuron-level-crossing) | Signed level-crossing (send-on-delta) event encoder, for RA. |
| [`MQIF`](#neuron-mqif) | Modified quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (batched PyTorch). |
| [`SA`](#neuron-sa) | Simplified Silicon (SA) neuron, faithful to paper eq.8 in normalized form. |
| [`sigma_delta`](#neuron-sigma-delta) | Sigma-delta (non-leaky integrate-and-fire, subtractive reset), for SA. |

### `AdEx` { #neuron-adex }

Adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire neuron (batched PyTorch).

Class: `sensoryforge.neurons.adex.AdExNeuronTorch`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EL` | float | `-70` | -100 to -40 | `mV` | Leak reversal potential |
| `VT` | float | `-50` | -80 to -20 | `mV` | Spike threshold (exponential term) |
| `DeltaT` | float | `2` | 0.1 to 10 | `mV` | Slope factor of the exponential term |
| `tau_m` | float | `20` | 1 to 200 | `ms` | Membrane time constant |
| `tau_w` | float | `100` | 1 to 500 | `ms` | Adaptation time constant |
| `a` | float | `2` | 0 to 20 |  | Subthreshold adaptation coupling |
| `b` | float | `0` | 0 to 20 |  | Spike-triggered adaptation increment |
| `v_reset` | float | `-58` | -100 to 0 | `mV` | Post-spike reset voltage |
| `v_spike` | float | `20` | -20 to 60 | `mV` | Spike detection voltage |
| `R` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 20 |  | Membrane resistance |
| `t_ref` *(advanced)* | float | `0` | 0 to 20 | `ms` | Absolute refractory period |
| `v_init` | float | `-70` | -100 to 50 | `mV` | Initial membrane voltage (default: EL) |
| `w_init` | float | `0` | -20 to 20 |  | Initial adaptation current |
| `dt` | float | `0.05` | 0.001 to 5 | `ms` | Integration time step |
| `noise_std` | float | `0` | 0 to 20 | `mV/sqrt(ms)` | Additive Langevin noise intensity on v |
| `v_floor` *(advanced)* | float | `null` | -200 to -50 | `mV` | Voltage floor (clamp); auto means no clamp |

Notes:

- `t_ref`: After a spike the voltage is held at v_reset for this long while the adaptation current keeps evolving. The SA1/RA1 presets use 2 ms, which caps the rate near 500 Hz.
- `v_floor`: Unset by default. Set it (e.g. -130.0 mV) to clamp v from below when integrating strongly negative input at a coarse step.

### `level_crossing` { #neuron-level-crossing }

Signed level-crossing (send-on-delta) event encoder, for RA.

Class: `sensoryforge.neurons.event_encoders.LevelCrossingNeuron`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `theta` | float | `1` | 1e-06 to 1000000 | `mA` | Level-crossing threshold: the input change per event |
| `refractory_ms` | float | `0` | 0 to 1000 | `ms` | Minimum interval between two events (0 = none) |
| `initial_reference` *(advanced)* | str | `"zero"` | one of `zero`, `first` |  | Reference at t = 0: 0, or the first input sample |
| `noise_std` *(advanced)* | float | `0` | 0 to 1000000 | `mA` | Comparator noise added to the input each step |
| `reference_leak_tau_ms` *(advanced)* | float | `null` | 0.001 to 1000000 | `ms` | Reference leak (unset = none, the v1.2.1 unit) |

Notes:

- `theta`: An ON event is emitted each time the drive has risen by theta since the last event, an OFF event each time it has fallen by theta; the reference moves by theta per event.
- `reference_leak_tau_ms`: After each step's events the reference relaxes toward the input by dt / tau, so a held level is forgotten and only changes faster than theta / tau make events. Must be at least the integration step.

## Filters { #filter }

Written as the `filter_method` of a population.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`identity`](#filter-identity), `none` | No filter |
| [`RA`](#filter-ra), `rafilter` | Rapidly adapting filter implementing Parvizi–Fard Equation 8. |
| [`SA`](#filter-sa), `safilter` | Slowly adapting filter implementing Parvizi–Fard Equations 6 and 7. |

### `identity` / `none` { #filter-identity }

No filter: the registry holds `None` under these names.

### `RA` / `rafilter` { #filter-ra }

Rapidly adapting filter implementing Parvizi–Fard Equation 8.

Class: `sensoryforge.filters.sa_ra.RAFilterTorch`

Registered under more than one name: `RA`, `rafilter`. They select the same class.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tau_RA` | float | `8` | 0.1 to 200 | `ms` | Adaptation time constant (ms); 8 ms follows Kandel Ch. 21. |
| `k3` | float | `2` | 0 to 200 |  | Gain applied to the rectified input derivative. |

### `SA` / `safilter` { #filter-sa }

Slowly adapting filter implementing Parvizi–Fard Equations 6 and 7.

Class: `sensoryforge.filters.sa_ra.SAFilterTorch`

Registered under more than one name: `SA`, `safilter`. They select the same class.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tau_r` | float | `5` | 0.1 to 200 | `ms` | Rise time constant (ms) governing auxiliary state dynamics. |
| `tau_d` | float | `30` | 0.1 to 500 | `ms` | Decay time constant (ms) governing output current dynamics. |
| `k1` | float | `0.05` | 0 to 10 |  | Gain applied to the input current (equation 7). |
| `k2` | float | `8` | 0 to 20 |  | Gain applied to the derivative term (equation 7). |
| `clip_to_positive` *(advanced)* | bool | `false` |  |  | Clamp the output I_SA to [0, inf) (non-physiological negative output otherwise possible). |

## Stimuli { #stimulus }

Written as the `type` of the `stimulus`.

The `layered` stimulus is built from the shapes, patterns, motions and modulations in the [World Language Reference](world_language.md); [Designing stimuli](../user_guide/designing_stimuli.md) explains how.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`braille`](#stimulus-braille) | A braille cell sliding along the y axis. |
| [`composite`](#stimulus-composite) | Composition of multiple stimuli with configurable combination mode. |
| [`drifting_grating`](#stimulus-drifting-grating) | A sinusoidal grating drifting along x, simulating a textured scan. |
| [`edge_grating`](#stimulus-edge-grating) | PyTorch module for generating edge grating stimuli. |
| [`gabor`](#stimulus-gabor), `texture` | PyTorch module for generating Gabor texture stimuli. |
| [`gaussian`](#stimulus-gaussian) | PyTorch module for generating Gaussian stimuli. |
| [`layered`](#stimulus-layered) | A stack of layers (see the module docstring); registered as `layered`. |
| [`moving`](#stimulus-moving) | Stimulus with temporal motion trajectory. |
| [`moving_edge`](#stimulus-moving-edge) | An oriented edge sweeping from `start` to `end` during the plateau. |
| [`ramp_gaussian`](#stimulus-ramp-gaussian) | Gaussian blob ramping to full amplitude then holding. |
| [`repeated_pattern`](#stimulus-repeated-pattern) | Tile a base stimulus on an N×M grid with configurable spacing. |
| [`static`](#stimulus-static) | Static spatial stimulus without temporal dynamics. |
| [`timeline`](#stimulus-timeline) | Composite stimulus with per-sub-stimulus onset, duration, and envelope. |

### `gabor` / `texture` { #stimulus-gabor }

PyTorch module for generating Gabor texture stimuli.

Class: `sensoryforge.stimuli.texture.GaborTexture`

Registered under more than one name: `gabor`, `texture`. They select the same class.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `center_x` | float | `0` | -20 to 20 | `mm` |  |
| `center_y` | float | `0` | -20 to 20 | `mm` |  |
| `amplitude` | float | `1` | 0 to 500 | `mA` |  |
| `sigma` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 20 | `mm` |  |
| `wavelength` | float | `1` | 0.01 to 10 | `mm` |  |
| `orientation` | float | `0` | 0 to 6.2832 | `rad` |  |
| `phase` | float | `0` | 0 to 6.2832 | `rad` |  |
| `signed` *(advanced)* | bool | `false` |  |  | Signed, zero-mean Gabor with negative lobes. |

Notes:

- `signed`: Off (default): a pressure, never negative -- amplitude x Gaussian window x (1 + cos(carrier)) / 2, peaking at the amplitude on the centre stripe. On: restores the signed, zero-mean form amplitude x window x cos(carrier), whose lobes between the stripes are negative, e.g. for signed contrast in vision. A negative pressure drives a negative current through the filters.

## Solvers { #solver }

Written as the `type` of a population's `solver_config`, or of the `solver` of the `simulation`.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`adaptive`](#solver-adaptive) | Adaptive ODE solver using torchdiffeq or torchode. |
| [`euler`](#solver-euler) | Forward Euler method for ODE integration. |

### `adaptive` { #solver-adaptive }

Adaptive ODE solver using torchdiffeq or torchode.

Class: `sensoryforge.solvers.adaptive.AdaptiveSolver`

It declares no `ParamSpec`; these are its constructor arguments.

| Argument | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `dt` |  | `0.05` |
| `method` |  | `"dopri5"` |
| `rtol` |  | `1e-05` |
| `atol` |  | `1e-07` |

### `euler` { #solver-euler }

Forward Euler method for ODE integration.

Class: `sensoryforge.solvers.euler.EulerSolver`

It declares no `ParamSpec`; these are its constructor arguments.

| Argument | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `dt` |  | `0.05` |

## Receptive-field builders { #innervation }

Written as the `innervation_method` of a population, or the `method` of an input's `rf`.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`distance_weighted`](#innervation-distance-weighted) | Distance-weighted innervation with mean connections and decay function. |
| [`gaussian`](#innervation-gaussian) | Gaussian-weighted random innervation (existing method). |
| [`imported`](#innervation-imported) | Receptive fields loaded from a CSV folder, a `.pt` bank or an `.npz`. |
| [`one_to_one`](#innervation-one-to-one) | One-to-one: each neuron connects to exactly K nearest receptors. |
| [`template`](#innervation-template) | Designed receptive fields: one Gaussian template on a square lattice. |
| [`uniform`](#innervation-uniform) | Uniform nearest-neighbor innervation (Voronoi-like). |

### `distance_weighted` { #innervation-distance-weighted }

Distance-weighted innervation with mean connections and decay function.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.innervation.DistanceWeightedInnervation`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connections_per_neuron` | float | `28` | 1 to 10000 |  | Mean number of receptors each neuron samples. |
| `sigma_d_mm` | float | `0.3` | 0.001 to 50 | `mm` | Width (sigma) of the receptive field's distance profile. |
| `max_distance_mm` | float | `1` | 0 to 100 | `mm` | Receptors farther than this from the neuron centre are not connected. |
| `decay_function` | str | `"exponential"` | one of `exponential`, `linear`, `inverse_square` |  | How a connection's weight falls with distance. |
| `decay_rate` | float | `2` | 0 to 100 |  | Rate of the distance decay. |
| `distance_weight_randomness_pct` *(advanced)* | float | `0` | 0 to 100 | `%` | Random jitter added to distance weights. |

### `gaussian` { #innervation-gaussian }

Gaussian-weighted random innervation (existing method).

Class: `sensoryforge.core.innervation.GaussianInnervation`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connections_per_neuron` | float | `28` | 1 to 10000 |  | Mean number of receptors each neuron samples. |
| `sigma_d_mm` | float | `0.3` | 0.001 to 50 | `mm` | Width (sigma) of the receptive field's distance profile. |
| `use_distance_weights` | bool | `false` |  |  | Weight each connection by its distance (analytic) instead of at random. |
| `far_connection_fraction` *(advanced)* | float | `0` | 0 to 1 |  | Fraction of connections drawn from a wider profile. |
| `far_sigma_factor` *(advanced)* | float | `5` | 1 to 100 |  | Width of the wider profile, as a multiple of sigma. |
| `distance_weight_randomness_pct` *(advanced)* | float | `0` | 0 to 100 | `%` | Random jitter added to distance weights. |

### `imported` { #innervation-imported }

Receptive fields loaded from a CSV folder, a `.pt` bank or an `.npz`.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.rf_builders.imported.ImportedRFBuilder`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | str | `""` |  |  | CSV export folder, .pt bank file, or .npz ConstructedRF file to import receptive fields from. |

### `one_to_one` { #innervation-one-to-one }

One-to-one: each neuron connects to exactly K nearest receptors.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.innervation.OneToOneInnervation`

It declares no `ParamSpec`; these are its constructor arguments.

| Argument | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `receptor_coords` | yes |  |
| `neuron_centers` | yes |  |
| `connections_per_neuron` |  | `28` |
| `sigma_d_mm` |  | `0.3` |
| `weight_range` |  | *not shown* |
| `use_distance_weights` |  | `true` |
| `far_connection_fraction` |  | `0` |
| `far_sigma_factor` |  | `5` |
| `max_distance_mm` |  | `1` |
| `decay_function` |  | `"exponential"` |
| `decay_rate` |  | `2` |
| `distance_weight_randomness_pct` |  | `0` |
| `seed` |  | `null` |
| `device` |  | `"cpu"` |

### `template` { #innervation-template }

Designed receptive fields: one Gaussian template on a square lattice.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.rf_builders.template.TemplateRFBuilder`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `resolvable_distance_mm` | float | `0.4` | 0.01 to 50 | `mm` | Resolvable distance d: sigma = d/pi, pitch = d. |
| `k` | int | `28` | 1 to 10000 |  | Nearest receptors kept per neuron. |
| `normalize` *(advanced)* | str | `"l2"` | one of `none`, `l2`, `sum` |  | Row normalization: unit-L2 (default), sum-to-one or none. |
| `weight_scale` *(advanced)* | float | `1` | 0 to 1000000 |  | Multiplier applied after normalization. |
| `edge_offset_mm` *(advanced)* | float | `null` | 0 to 50 | `mm` | Lattice inset from the receptor box (default pitch/2). |

| `decay_function` | str | `"exponential"` | one of `exponential`, `linear`, `inverse_square` |  | How a connection's weight falls with distance. |

| Name | What it is |

### `identity` { #processing-identity }

Pass-through layer — returns input unchanged.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.processing.IdentityLayer`

It takes no parameters.

### `onoff` { #processing-onoff }

Centre-surround ON/OFF split over receptor coordinates.

Class: `sensoryforge.core.processing.OnOffLayer`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Range | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sigma_center_mm` | float | `0.15` | 0.001 to 10 | `mm` | Centre Gaussian standard deviation of the DoG kernel. |
| `sigma_surround_mm` | float | `0.45` | 0.001 to 20 | `mm` | Surround Gaussian standard deviation of the DoG kernel. |
